answer: At epoch close, each agent submits a receipt detailing the copper they mined and the meadow they cleared. Verifier checks receipts against a ledger, ensuring that each copper corresponds to a unique meadow, preventing cloning by imposing a cost of 100 copper per ledger entry. An attacker with 2000 receipts must mine 200,000 copper, losing 1,900 copper to clear the same 200 meadows, making cloning unprofitable.
